cases.statement: One female, Case 2 (PMID 31660500), with arrhythmias from childhood and dilated cardiomyopathy after pregnancy.

people.label: Case 2
people.key_phenotypes: ventricular tachycardias since early childhood; atrial tachycardias and pre-excitation; LVEF fell to 38% in pregnancy with dilated cardiomyopathy and late enhancement on CMR; atrial fibrillation; retinopathy; normal neurological evaluation

quotes.quote: Case 2 was 25 years of age when a LAMP-2 mutation was found.
Her medical history revealed incessant complex ventricular tachycardias since early childhood.
The electrogram showed signs of pre-excitation (Figure 1B) with a positive deltawave in the inferior leads and negative T waves in the anterior leads.
She became pregnant at the age of 24 and her left ventricular ejection fraction, which had been normal before pregnancy, reduced to 38%.
Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple areas of late enhancement.
Neurological evaluation was within normal limits, but signs of retinopathy were found by the ophthalmologist.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Cardiac and retinal findings in a female; a 53-gene cardiomyopathy panel found no other relevant variant. Family history negative for cardiac disorders.

quotes.quote: Targeted sequencing of 53 cardiomyopathy-related genes identified a frameshift mutation, c.966dup p.(Ala323Cysfs*27), in the LAMP2 gene. No additional relevant mutations/variants were identified in the other 52 genes.
Case 2 was referred for genetic testing at 25 years of age. The family history was negative for cardiac disorders.
On ophthalmologic examination, all three had retinal pigment changes consistent with Danon disease

segregation.statement: Not reported. The only family information is a negative family history for cardiac disorders.

quotes.quote: Case 2 was referred for genetic testing at 25 years of age. The family history was negative for cardiac disorders.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide duplication causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Ala323CysfsTer27), as written in the paper). The paper states LAMP2 deficiency as the disease mechanism.

quotes.quote: The gene defect underlying Danon disease causes a deficiency of lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call the LAMP2 variants in all three cases causal; Alamut and Cartagenia were used for classification, with no criteria given.

quotes.quote: In all three cases, a final diagnosis of Danon disease was only made after genetic testing that identified a causal variant in the lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 gene.
This software was used in combination with the Alamut software (Interactive Biosoftware, Rouen, France) for variant filtering and classification.

concerns: Transcript stated as NM_002294.2; the batch uses NM_002294.3.

PMID 31660500 contradicts itself on pre-excitation in Case 2: the case text describes signs of pre-excitation, the discussion says Case 2 had no clear signs of pre-excitation and names Cases 1 and 3 instead. The discussion also says 'As Case 2 illustrated, mechanical support is sometimes needed', which matches Case 1's history.
No parental or relative testing is reported.
notes_for_panel: Single female case with a frameshift, panel-negative for 52 other cardiomyopathy genes, with retinopathy; no segregation data.
